privacy-policy: Please read these Conditions of use (“terms”) carefully before using this website. Accessing, browsing or using this website is a privilege subject to the following Terms and indicates your agreement and acceptance of these Terms. By using this website you acknowledge that you have read, understood and agree to the following terms.
Information we collect and how we use it Personal Information

You may choose to provide personal information (such as your name, address, telephone number and email address) on this web site. We ask you for information such as your name and email address so we can respond to your questions and comments. If you would like to receive AACCI news alerts, we ask for your name and email address so we can send you the news alerts.

On www.asianafrican.org, we provide a phone number, a postal address and an email address so visitors can report complaints about quality assurance standards or other concerns to the Asian-African Chamber of Commerce & Industry Foundation. If you email us, please be aware that you will be providing us with your email address and any other information you include in your email.
Use of Cookies and Similar Technologies

Like most companies we use cookies on our websites. We collect certain aggregate and non-personal information through a variety of technologies when you visit this website. Aggregate and non-personal information does not relate to a single identifiable visitor. It tells us such things as how many users visited our site and the pages accessed. By collecting this information, we learn how to best tailor our website to our visitors. Unless you disable such technologies, by using our website and online services, you agree that we can place these types of cookies and related technologies on your device. We explain below how you can manage your choices and opt-out of the collection of such aggregate information.
Some cookies serve an essential function and the websites cannot work properly without them. Where such essential cookies are used, they cannot be disabled.

Other cookies serve a functional purpose and improve the user experience of the websites. We use browser and Flash cookies to tell us, for example, whether you’ve visited us before, and to help us identify site features in which you may have the greatest interest. Browser and Flash cookies may enhance your online experience by saving your preferences while you are visiting a particular site so that you do not need to reset them each time you visit the website. Neither Browser nor Flash cookies can identify you as an individual. You can decline any Browser cookie through your browser however, without Browser cookies you may not be able to take full advantage of all our website features.

We do not sell or otherwise disclose personal information about our web site visitors, except as described here. We may share information provided by our visitors to service providers we have retained to perform services on our behalf. These service providers are contractually restricted from using or disclosing the information except as necessary to perform services on our behalf or to comply with legal requirements. In addition, we may disclose information about you (i) if we are required to do so by law or legal process, (ii) to law enforcement authorities or other government officials, or (iii) when we believe disclosure is necessary or appropriate to prevent physical harm or financial loss or in connection with an investigation of suspected or actual illegal activity. We reserve the right to transfer any information we have about you in the event we sell or transfer all or a portion of our business or assets. Should such a sale or transfer occur, we will use reasonable efforts to direct the transferee to use personal information you have provided through this web site in a manner that is consistent with this Privacy Statement.

We may transfer the personal information we collect on this site to other countries where we do quality assurance certification accreditation & ratings services, but we will do so only for the purposes described above. When we transfer your information to other countries, we will protect that information as described here unless otherwise required by applicable laws.

To keep personally identifiable information that you provide via this site accurate, current, and complete, please contact us and we will take appropriate steps to update or correct such information in our possession, or to delete your information from our contact list.

code-of-conduct: AACCI individual members and those representing organizational membership, which shall now onwards be used as AACCI members, shall at all times maintain the Integrity Code of AACCI Membership, especially in public. A member shall:
Always be a gentleman (or a lady).
Be respectful of others, particularly other members.
Respect the laws of the respective society, community, state and country.
Never exemplify bad behavior in public.
Not be under the influence of drinks or drugs or overly drunk in public where their representation as a AACCI member damages AACCI’s reputation.
Dress with dignity when representing or being recognized as part of AACCI.
Be civil in disagreements, especially with other AACCI members.
Willingness to assist your brother or sisters (other members) in society.
Membership fees to be paid and renewed on time.
Membership is not transferrable and is not usable by anyone other than the member.

Death of a Member: In case of individual membership, entitles his or her son or daughter to assume his or her membership, provided he or she qualifies to be a member of AACCI; or in case of organizational membership, urges the organization to appoint another representative.

AACCI requires verifiable Government Issued ID, which may be a Driving License or passport copy in case of individual members or company registration papers in case of organizational membership, before authorizing membership and may ask such ID to be updated with AACCI prior to expiration of such ID. All information provided to AACCI will be protected and not available to any individual or business or government agency without a legal order from a court of proper jurisdiction.

Any AACCI Member found to have intentionally committed any of the following acts or found guilty of any such act, either prior to applying for membership but not disclosing such information, or such act was committed after membership was granted, shall have their membership immediately revoked: larceny, theft, robbery, kidnapping, terrorism, embezzlement, counterfeiting, aggravated assault, murder, arson, bribery, child pornography, child abuse, fraud (any type that exceeds misdemeanour level), illegal drug dealing or trafficking or manufacturing or distribution or transportation, forgery, money laundering or rape.
A member shall be responsible for any damage he/she has caused or created when involved in a AACCI sponsored event or when representing AACCI or presenting himself as a AACCI Member.

Members shall not remove any property belonging to AACCI or a vendor, supplier, other member, agent, employee or representative of AACCI from any AACCI sponsored event or event sponsored by AACCI vendors, suppliers or related events.

Any member found to bring a firearm or a sharp edged weapon that could be used for bodily harm to a AACCI event as a representative of AACCI or recognized publicly as a AACCI member shall have his/her membership immediately revoked.

Members attending an AACCI event or when representing AACCI at other events shall not be disruptive, aggressive, violent, threatening, have rude or boisterous behavior or other actions that are unbecoming of a member representing AACCI.
Members shall not be aggressive or overly aggressive with the opposite sex or with other members. Consistent violation of this shall constitute a violation of the code.
Members shall not be deemed to be financially irresponsible or repeated delinquent on any debt owed to AACCI.

Members shall not use, represent, hold events in the name of or hold themselves out to be an agent, officer, executive or owner of – the AACCI, its name, logo, property, have an access to its offices or other false information that exceeds its rights as members as are provided in writing on this website.

Members shall not duplicate the AACCI logos, trademarks or images on to paper, clothing, products, boats, cars, motorcycles or any other place or surface that are not authorized prints or images without the express written consent of AACCI.

Members shall not submit, cause to be submitted or be involved in or assist with the submission of any news, report, public announcement that is printed, written, produced on any form of news, social media, online news service, public media or another manner of submission or posting that is for public or large audience access or visibility – without prior written approval by a AACCI by it’s President / CEO.
AACCI, in general and specifically at AACCI sponsored or advertised events – is not liable or responsible for:
Damage to possessions, including auto, bike, car, etc. and including technology equipment, recreational equipment and other physical possessions.
The theft of intellectual property, documents, files, other mediums of information.
Any damages caused by the use of Valets or other similar services.

AACCI shall have the unilateral right, without notice, to adopt new Rules & Requirements and amend them at any time and from time to time. Any disputes or ambiguities regarding the interpretation of these Rules & Requirements shall be resolved by AACCI. The exercise of any right, power, privilege, or authority that may be exercised by AACCI pursuant to these Rules& Requirements, and any determination, approval or other action that may be taken by AACCI pursuant to these Rules& Requirements, may be exercised or taken at the sole and absolute discretion of AACCI.
Interpretation of these Rules & Requirements shall be entirely held by AACCI.
All disputes shall be addressed to a court in the city of Ahmedabad, Gujarat state, India only.
All individuals associated with the AACCI chapter office shall conduct themselves with the highest ethical standards, promoting honesty, integrity, and fairness in all business practices.
Avoid conflicts of interest and act in the best interests of the chamber and its members.
Maintain a professional demeanour in all interactions, both within the chamber and with external stakeholders.
Treat all individuals with respect and professionalism, irrespective of their background or affiliation.
Safeguard confidential information shared within the chamber, including member data, financial information, and other sensitive materials.
Maintain strict confidentiality unless legally obligated to disclose information or with explicit consent.
Utilize AACCI resources, including office facilities, equipment, and intellectual property, solely for official purposes and in a responsible manner.
Seek appropriate authorization before using chamber resources for personal or external purposes.

careers: Role Overview: The Sales Manager plays a pivotal role in driving growth, revenue, and strategic partnerships for the Chamber. They lead a dynamic team, focusing on membership expansion, financial sustainability, and enhancing the Chamber’s influence.
Membership Growth: Develop and execute strategies to expand the membership base by converting leads into new members.
Revenue Generation: Achieve revenue targets through sales of memberships, sponsorships, and advertising opportunities.
Member Engagement: Foster member satisfaction, engagement, and renewals for a strong and loyal member community.
Strategic Partnerships: Identify and nurture partnerships with key organizations to enhance the Chamber’s reach and influence.
Event Success: Drive participation and sponsorship for Chamber events by engaging sponsors and encouraging member involvement.
Market Insights: Conduct market research, analyse trends, and identify new opportunities for effective sales strategies.
CRM Utilization: Optimize sales processes and customer relationships through effective use of CRM tools.
Reporting & Analysis: Provide comprehensive sales reports and insights to senior management for informed decision-making.
Brand Ambassador: Maintain a professional image while representing the Chamber to external stakeholders and the business community.
Team Leadership: Minimum 2 years of experience in Sales.
Effective Communication: Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Lead Generation: Proven experience in lead generation.
Social Media: Proficient in leveraging social media platforms.
Join us in driving the growth and influence of the Asian African Chamber of Commerce & Industry. Apply your expertise to shape our success!
Opportunity to connect with business owners and entrepreneurs. Attractive incentives tied to your performance, offering lucrative rewards.

Company Overview: Asian-African Chamber of Commerce & Industry Foundation (AACCI) is a registered private, non-stock corporation headquartered in Delaware, USA. Our mission is to serve as a catalyst for promoting trade and business between Asian and African regions, with a focus on supporting Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and industries. AACCI aims to foster economic growth and sustainable business practices through strategic alliances, trade facilitation, and policy advocacy.

Position Overview: We are seeking a dynamic and proactive individual to join our team as an Officer Strategic Alliance. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in driving partnerships, facilitating trade agreements, and advocating for policies that enhance economic cooperation between Asia and Africa.

Research and Analysis: Conduct research on market trends, investment opportunities, and trade regulations in Asian and African countries. Provide insights and analysis to AACCI members to support their business decision-making processes.

Partnership Development: Forge partnerships with relevant organizations, industry associations, and government agencies to strengthen AACCI’s network and influence. Identify strategic alliances that can enhance AACCI’s objectives and expand its reach.
Collecting information about Global Events & see how AACCI can participate / collaborate for the same.
Trade Facilitation: Facilitate trade agreements and partnerships between Asian and African businesses. Monitor trade trends between the two regions and identify opportunities for growth.

Event Management: Support to organize trade fairs, exhibitions, and networking events to promote business interactions among members. Ensure smooth execution of events and measure their effectiveness in fostering trade relations. Pre & Post event promotions on all social media of AACCI.
Policy Advocacy: Advocate for policies that promote trade and economic cooperation between Asia and Africa.
Identifying MOU Partners & Event Partners with logo support.
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, International Relations, Economics, or related field. Master’s degree preferred.
Proven experience in strategic alliance development, preferably in an international business environment.
Strong understanding of trade dynamics and regulations in Asian and African markets.
Excellent research and analytical skills with the ability to translate data into actionable insights.
Ability to work effectively in a multicultural and diverse team environment.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and familiarity with social media platforms.
Willingness to travel domestically and internationally, as required.

Join us in our mission to foster economic growth and sustainable business practices across Asia and Africa. If you are passionate about building strategic partnerships and driving impactful change, we invite you to apply for the Officer Strategic Alliance position at AACCI.

message-from-founder-chairman: p
Welcome and thank you for visiting the Asian-African Chamber of Commerce & Industry’s (AACCI) website!
p
I am elated to be the Founder and Chairman of AACCI. Our Board Advisory and Members consist of some very distinguished and pioneering individuals/organizations.
p

AACCI plays an integral part in the successful cultivation of a vibrant business community. As an organization, we are the voice of businesses, entrepreneurs and professionals in Asian & African regions.
p

Our principal mission as an inter-continental Chamber is to facilitate and foster economic growth for 102 countries in Asian & African region. The Chamber helps in the improvement of the business climate for the development of private investment, cultivate public-private dialogue, etc. AACCI is also active in capacity building for its members through organizing seminars, workshops and offers various platforms for members to exchange ideas and share experiences.
p
We recognize that a healthy business environment and a connected business community encourages businesses to grow, subsequently creating more jobs and opportunities for the people of Ascension.
p
Our commitment to our members is – ‘to be energized and passionate about our businesses and ultimately their successes’.
p
Currently, we offer lucrative membership pricing, networking opportunities, website and social media marketing, member-to-member discounts, annual business expo and much more.
p

In the coming future, we would be creating new committees within our group. These new committees will provide members with the marketing tools to promote their business through welcome packets, mailer newsletters, website and more. By working together to create an effective and purposeful business climate, we can grow and prosper.
p
I look forward to working with everyone who is associated with this chamber and wish a successful year to all businesses encompassed within our marketing area.
p

Feedback is important to us and will help us in our growth, thus, give us your kind feedback. If we are doing things that work for you, let us know. If there are things that we could improve, let us know. Together, we can make the Chamber of prosperity and growth.
p
I look forward to the upcoming challenges and opportunities that arise.
p
To our members, we thank you for your investment in our Chamber and appreciate all that you do for us. If you are not a chamber member, please consider joining and being a part of our mission.

objectives: To facilitate advocacy, dialogue and exchange of information between Members and the Member countries’ government officials and agencies in order to improve the business climate in the region, and to promote Asian business interests in African;

Public-private partnership in the development of projects and more particularly, regional projects covering more than one AACCI-member country.

AACCI is also active in capacity building for its members through the organization of seminars, workshops and offers various platforms for members to exchange ideas and share experiences.
body: AACCI is composed of the following organs:
The General Assembly as the supreme organ of the Chamber.

Permanent Secretariat consisting of the Founder Directors are also members of the General Assembly and are responsible for setting the policy and strategies for the Chamber. They will provide strategic inputs and directions for implementation.

There will be one permanent Secretariat supported by two Vice Chairmen for regulating activities: one in Lagos, Nigeria for the African region and similarly the Asian Secretariat at Sri Lanka, providing them advice and other networking support in running the chamber.
The Executive Council is responsible for the management of the Chamber which is based at Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India at the Asian Secretariat Hub
The Technical Commissions, technical bodies, are occasionally set up to review issues related to the deliberations of the Chamber
the-logo: First and foremost we would like to share that the logo of Asian-African Chamber of Commerce & Industry incorporates the Vision and ideals of its founder & president Dr. GD Singh, who, around 10 years back envisioned a dream of integrating the Asian and African region together on single platform of growth and equity.To coin the logo in one single word, it represents – Integration.
The three stripes represent the ideals upon which this organisation is build:

1.) Red – this colour has always depicted ‘power’ and ‘vigour’ among other things, at AACCI we see red as a sign of ‘solidity’ , the relentless probe of conjuring the apex among the services which a Chamber is manifested for being in existence.
2.) Green – denotes sustainability and eco-friendly organisations for an optimistic future where environment is kept as a ‘focal’ of activities with a unison aligned thought of preserving the nature.

3.) Orange – in many ancient civilizations this colour has been used synonymous with ‘prosperity’, whether from the Asian or African continent. We have imbibed this colour to our logo to indicate that we strive towards prosperity of the member nations and it SME industries through synergies and commerce.

The other two elements of the logo also hold significance, representing again the ideals and foundations of the two continents. The solid ‘A’ represents the entire the Asian economy having been boosted by first the Japanese growth, then by the tiger economies and now by India – China economic boom.

On the flipside, much of the African region is yet to realise an economic boom thus holding an immense potential of unexplored realms of exponential growth. Depicted by the continent’s map’s outline ending with an upward arrow.
The union of these two elements of the logo is the foundation of this Chamber – uniting the world economies for a sustainable, prosperous, progressive and solid future.

annual-general-meeting: An annual general meeting (commonly abbreviated as AGM, also known as the annual meeting) is a meeting of the general membership of an organisation. These organisations include membership associations and companies with shareholders.

The AGM may include electing a board of directors, making important decisions regarding the organisation, and informing the members of previous and future activities. At this meeting, the stakeholders and partners may receive copies of the company’s accounts, review fiscal information for the past year, and ask any questions regarding the directions the business will take in the future.

At the annual general meeting, the president or chairman of the organization presides over the meeting and may give an overall status of the organisation. The secretary prepares the minutes and may be asked to read important papers. The financial director may present a financial report. Other officers, the board of directors, and committees may give their reports. Attending this meeting are the members or the stakeholders of the organization.
newsletters: The Chamber Newsletter is sent out to all of our members quarterly.

We are also always looking for Chamber members who are interested in writing an article! You, as a business person, have useful, interesting, and thought provoking knowledge, information, and ideas. Why not share them with your fellow businesses? It’s a great way to get your name out there, form social connections, and inform fellow business owners of some of what’s made you so successful.

If your business has changed recently, is hosting an interesting event, or has a truly unique outlook on how it practices business, we can talk about doing a business profile to feature you in the newsletter. Due to time and space constraints, advertorial style articles which simply advertise your business cannot be accommodated right now. However, if you’d like to place an advertisement in the newsletter give a call to the office and we can get you set up with a paid advertising spot.

Please, don’t hesitate to contact us to get feedback on articles for possible inclusion in the newsletter. We will do some editing, so it doesn’t have to be perfect, but do your best to write clearly and professionally. Make sure your article has a title and a unifying theme, and is related either to your business or business generally. Personal and political pieces, while fascinating, aren’t appropriate for this particular publication.

Is there a topic you think we should be writing about, but you’re nervous about doing it yourself? Shoot us an email on asia@asianafrican.org for Asian members and africa@asianafrican.org for African members; perhaps we can co-author something together!

dangotes-16-billion-kenya-refinery-proje.title: Dangote’s $16 Billion Kenya Refinery Project
blocks: p

Dangote has officially begun construction of a massive $16 billion oil refinery project in Kenya, representing a significant investment in Africa’s energy and industrial infrastructure. The project is expected to strengthen Kenya’s energy security, reduce dependence on imported refined petroleum products, and create substantial opportunities across construction, logistics, manufacturing, and related industries.
p

The development also highlights the growing scale of African-led private-sector investment in strategic infrastructure and energy. As one of Africa’s most prominent industrial groups, Dangote’s expansion reflects the increasing importance of large-scale projects in driving economic growth, employment, trade, and regional development.
p

With Kenya serving as an important gateway to East Africa, the refinery could have wider implications for regional energy supply chains and economic integration. Such projects can create opportunities for local businesses, international investors, technology providers, contractors, and service companies across the continent.

zambias-copper-boom-a-new-era-of-mining-.title: Zambia’s Copper Boom: A New Era of Mining & Investment
blocks: p

Zambia is reaffirming its commitment to transforming its mining sector by aiming to triple annual copper production to 3 million tonnes, supported by more than US$10 billion in mining investments since 2021. As one of Africa’s richest copper-producing nations, Zambia is leveraging strong investor confidence, policy reforms, and strategic partnerships to unlock the full potential of its mineral resources.
p

Industry stakeholders are emphasizing the need for continued investment in mineral exploration, local processing facilities, transport infrastructure, renewable energy, and power generation to sustain long-term growth. Expanding domestic value addition and modernizing logistics will not only strengthen Zambia’s mining ecosystem but also increase export competitiveness and attract new global investors.
p

With the global shift toward electric vehicles, renewable energy, and advanced manufacturing driving unprecedented demand for copper, Zambia is uniquely positioned to become a key supplier of this critical mineral. The country’s ambitious mining strategy presents significant opportunities for businesses, investors, technology providers, and infrastructure developers across Africa and beyond.

ethiopias-us12-5-billion-bishoftu-intern.title: Ethiopia’s US$12.5 Billion Bishoftu International Airport Project Gains Global Momentum
blocks: p

Ethiopia is taking a transformative step toward becoming one of Africa’s leading aviation and logistics hubs with its ambitious US$12.5 billion Bishoftu International Airport project. The mega infrastructure development has already begun attracting global investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners, reflecting strong international confidence in Ethiopia’s long-term economic vision.
p

Designed to become one of Africa’s largest airports, the Bishoftu International Airport will dramatically increase passenger handling capacity while expanding cargo operations to support growing trade across Africa and beyond. The project is expected to strengthen Ethiopia’s position as a regional aviation gateway, improve supply chain connectivity, enhance tourism, facilitate international business, and generate substantial employment opportunities.
p

For businesses across Asia and Africa, the development presents significant opportunities in airport infrastructure, engineering, logistics, aviation services, construction, technology, hospitality, and foreign investment. It also reinforces Africa’s rapidly expanding infrastructure landscape and highlights the continent’s commitment to building world-class transport networks that support economic growth and regional integration.

aacci-director-general-m-j-puri-sets-out.title: AACCI Director General M. J. Puri sets out vision for cross-continental growth
blocks: p

Trade and investment between Asia and Africa will depend increasingly on stronger local networks, clearer regulation and closer cooperation between business and government, according to M. J. Puri, Director General of the Asia Africa Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
p

In a recent interview, Puri said the chamber’s purpose was rooted in long-term economic partnership. “AACCI serves as a strategic bridge between Asia and Africa, fostering trade, investment, entrepreneurship, technology transfer, and institutional collaboration,” he explained. “Our mission is to create sustainable economic partnerships and strengthen South-South cooperation.”That role is becoming more visible as businesses across Africa and Asia look for new markets, investment partners and supply chains. Puri said AACCI’s expansion strategy is being shaped by the need to work closer to the ground, particularly through national chapters that can connect local business communities with regional and international opportunities.
p

“Our growth is driven by the need for local engagement through country chapters that facilitate business networking, trade promotion, investment opportunities, and policy dialogue,” Puri told SiGMA News.
p

Through these country chapters, AACCI gives companies, chambers, investors and institutions a direct route into conversations that often stall because of distance, limited market knowledge or lack of trusted contacts.
p
Agriculture, energy and technology among priority sectors
p
Puri said the scope for cooperation is not confined to one industry, with opportunities spread across both established sectors and fast-growing digital fields.
p

“Agriculture, renewable energy, manufacturing, infrastructure, healthcare, tourism, education, fintech, AI, logistics, and digital transformation remain the strongest sectors for collaboration,” he said.
p

The list reflects the scale of economic overlap between the two regions. Many African economies are seeking investment in infrastructure, industrialisation, healthcare and digital services, while Asian companies are looking for new partnerships, production bases and growth markets. AACCI says its role is to bring those interests into a more structured framework.The Director General also acknowledged that the opportunity is not without obstacles. “Information gaps, financing constraints, logistics challenges, regulatory complexity, and limited institutional connectivity,” he said, were among the main barriers limiting cooperation.
p

He said AACCI works to address those barriers “through partnerships and trade facilitation.”Puri stressed that governments and businesses cannot build these links alone. “It is essential,” he said of cross-sector collaboration. “Governments, businesses, academia, and development institutions must work together to create sustainable economic growth.”
p
Startups and digital industries move into focus
p

AACCI is also looking closely at entrepreneurs, startups and emerging digital sectors. Puri said the chamber supports entrepreneurs “through networking, international exposure, investor access, mentorship, trade missions, and business development platforms.”That support is likely to become more important as smaller companies and technology-led businesses seek access to investors and cross-border networks. Puri said gaming, entertainment and technology are becoming more important economic sectors.“These sectors are becoming major economic contributors through innovation, digital transformation, job creation, and technology adoption,” he said.
p

He added that AACCI could help build responsible growth in these areas by bringing together different players. “AACCI can facilitate dialogue among investors, regulators, technology providers, and entrepreneurs to support responsible growth,” he argued.Regulation, he suggested, will be central to whether fast-growing sectors can attract confidence and capital. “Transparency, compliance, and responsible governance are fundamental to sustainable industry growth and investor confidence,” he said.Looking ahead, Puri said AACCI’s ambition is clear: “To become the leading Asia-Africa business bridge that drives trade, investment, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development across both continents.”
p

For AACCI, that means continuing to build platforms where business leaders, investors, entrepreneurs, chambers and institutions can meet, exchange ideas and turn regional potential into practical partnerships.Source : Asia-Africa cooperation could unlock new gaming opportunities
